readingPlans.title: 7-Day Introduction to the Gita
readingPlans.subtitle: One short reading a day, for a week
readingPlans.description: A week-long first pass. Each day is one or two verses and a question, chosen so that by the end you have met the problem the Gita is answering, its central instruction, and enough of its vocabulary to keep reading on your own.

days.title: Why the Gita begins on a battlefield
days.intro: Before any teaching, there is a person who cannot act. Read the opening and notice that the problem is stated at full strength before anyone answers it.
days.reflection: What decision are you currently avoiding, and what makes every option feel wrong?

days.title: What does not change
days.intro: The first substantive answer is about what persists through change.
days.reflection: What in you feels continuous between the person you were at ten and the person reading this?

days.title: The central instruction
days.intro: The most quoted verse in the Gita, and the easiest to misread as indifference.
days.reflection: Name one piece of work where you are carrying both the effort and the verdict. What would it change to carry only the first?

days.title: How wanting becomes anger
days.intro: A short causal chain that repays slow reading.
days.reflection: Trace one recent flash of anger backwards. Where did it actually start?

days.title: Your work, not someone else's
days.intro: Svadharma: the Gita's answer to comparison.
days.reflection: Whose life are you measuring yours against, and is that comparison telling you anything true?

days.title: Lift yourself by yourself
days.intro: The Gita's most self-reliant verse, from the chapter on meditation.
days.reflection: In what area are you currently your own enemy?

days.title: Where this leaves you
days.intro: Look back over the week. The Gita does not end in agreement; it ends in a decision.
days.reflection: What is one thing you will do differently this week, and what result are you willing to stop guaranteeing yourself?

readingPlans.subtitle: The whole Gita, at a chapter a day
readingPlans.description: The complete text in eighteen sittings. About twenty minutes a day, more for the longer chapters. Best attempted after a shorter plan, or alongside a commentary.

readingPlans.title: 21 Days of Karma Yoga
readingPlans.subtitle: Working without being ruled by results
readingPlans.description: Three weeks on the Gita's teaching about action. Deliberately repetitive: the verses return, and the reflection questions change. The aim is to make one idea usable, not to cover ground.

days.title: Action cannot be avoided
days.intro: Start from the observation that nobody is ever inactive.
days.reflection: List everything you did today that you would not call 'work'. Was any of it inaction?

days.title: The claim on the action
days.intro: Read 2.47 again, slowly, one clause at a time.
days.reflection: Which of the four clauses is hardest for you?

days.title: What attachment costs
days.intro: The chain from dwelling to anger.
days.reflection: What have you been dwelling on this week?

days.title: Your own work
days.intro: Svadharma against paradharma.
days.reflection: What work is genuinely yours right now?

days.title: Effort without guarantee
days.intro: Holding effort and outcome apart in practice.
days.reflection: Where are you withholding effort because the outcome is uncertain?

days.title: The self as friend
days.intro: Self-effort as the mechanism.
days.reflection: What would treating yourself as an ally look like today?

days.title: Review
days.intro: Look back at the first week.
days.reflection: What has shifted, if anything?

days.title: Day 8
days.intro: Continue with the verses from the first week, in the order that is most useful to you. Repetition is the point of this plan, not novelty.

readingPlans.title: Gita for Stress
readingPlans.subtitle: Ten short readings for a heavy period

days.title: What is yours to carry
days.intro: The separation of effort from outcome.
days.reflection: Write down what you are carrying. Mark which parts you actually control.

days.title: Where the pressure starts
days.intro: Dwelling, attachment, wanting.
days.reflection: What has your mind been circling?

days.title: Do not let yourself sink
days.intro: Self-effort, stated plainly.
days.reflection: What is one small thing that would make tomorrow slightly easier?
